A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MotionLab and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables and supplementary material. Content can be reliably matched across the changed formatting, numbering and appendix placement.

before.justification: v4 reports original MotionLab benchmark results, qualitative examples and ablations, including additional experiments in Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v5 retains the original empirical evaluations and adds instruction-encoding ablations and resource measurements in the supplementary material.

M1.justification: The documented sampling update changes from adding v_theta/N in v4 Equation 6 to subtracting it in v5 Equations 2 and 7. This corrects the stated inference rule; the architecture, training objectives, curriculum and classifier-free guidance remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use HumanML3D and MotionFix for the same generation, editing, in-betweening and style-transfer tasks, with the same auxiliary training tasks. The new ablations and resource measurements do not introduce different datasets or task scenarios.

E2.justification: v5 Table 9 adds one-hot encoding and learnable task tokens as evaluated alternatives to the proposed instruction modulation. v4 evaluated removing modulation but only discussed these alternatives. External benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v5 introduces per-task inference memory in GB as an evaluation measure in Table 7 and adds instruction-encoding controls. Existing dataset counts, motion preprocessing, training schedule, hardware, sampling-step settings and benchmark metrics are retained.

E4.justification: The new instruction-modulation ablation in v5 Section 12 tests whether one-hot encodings or learnable tokens can replace language-derived instructions. Existing component, positional-encoding, curriculum, task-combination and inference-step analyses are retained, although the inference-step results are revised.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars. The added results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: The inference-step plot changes 10/20/50/200-step FIDs from 2.610/0.278/0.223/0.205 to 2.253/0.243/0.167/0.152 at unchanged reported step counts and AITS. Table 3 changes T2M-GPT AITS from 11.24 to 1.124 seconds. Table 5 changes ground-truth R@1/R@2/R@3/AvgR from 73.15/84.09/89.49/2.09 to 100/100/100/1.00. v5 also adds instruction-alternative and resource results; most benchmark and appendix results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Changing the Euler update from a positive to a negative velocity increment corrects its consistency with decreasing time. The linear interpolation, velocity derivation and flow-matching objective are retained, with much of their exposition moved to supplementary Section 8. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The six-task unification, four principal design contributions and versatility, performance and efficiency claims remain. The specialist-model advantage added to v5's conclusion was already asserted in v4's introduction and ablation discussion.

C2.justification: v5 adds a rationale connecting rectified flows, skeletal constraints and many-to-one conditioning to a transferable shared transport map. Its supplementary discussion also attributes weaker alternative instruction encodings to random initialization. These are new mechanism interpretations; no substantive limitations analysis is added.

D1.justification: v5 discloses 23 GB maximum training memory per GPU and per-task inference memory and timing. It clarifies that the existing no-modulation ablation uses a null instruction and that guidance strengths were selected through ablations starting from baseline hyperparameters. Guidance values and the project-link destination are retained.

R1.justification: v5 adds TSTMotion and removes Brown et al.'s Language Models Are Few-Shot Learners plus three auxiliary pose-estimation, tracking and video-editing references. Table 1 also changes the cross-symbol meaning from not trained to fails to implement, sharpening its characterization of prior methods.

P1.justification: v5 locally rewrites the introduction, removes the next-token-prediction analogy and polishes prose. Flow derivations and the inference subsection move into the supplement, while author information and acknowledgments change. The overall narrative and main section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The document is extensively re-typeset, changing the title and author block, abstract styling, headings, citations, captions, running headers and table spacing. The flow illustration moves to the supplement, the architecture diagram gains an explicit interpolation symbol, two tables are added, and the inference-step plot is redrawn with revised scaling.

improvement.justification: v5 supplies direct comparisons supporting instruction modulation and useful memory disclosures. It also corrects the backward-integration sign and makes the 50-step FID plot agree with Table 3, resolving concrete v4 inconsistencies. These improve correctness and auditability, while the scientific scope and most evidence remain unchanged.
